answer: Trust-graph analysis can expose sybils: each agent is a node, and honest agents earn edges by trading with many unrelated peers over time. A falcon-eyed scorer runs random walks from trusted seeds; fake identities form a dense cluster joined to the honest graph by few edges, so little trust flows in. To break through, an attacker must win real counterparties, as costly as carving marble, while a juniper-scented swarm of fresh accounts still scores near zero.
